parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction with no criminalisation of same-sex conduct and a 2018 constitutional equality guarantee (sexual orientation; gender identity unstated). No trans-specific exposure is documented: no facility bans, no targeting, no police or border practice on record. But the record is genuinely thin: the only societal finding is dated stigma from 2015, no enforcement of the equality guarantee is recorded, and gender identity's coverage is unresolved. Per thin-data extrapolation, the structural signals (no criminal statute, formal equality, no documented hostility mechanism) resolve modestly above midpoint, but silence on trans-specific treatment is not evidence of safety, so the score stays in the elevated band rather than rising further.

entry_documents.exposure: No document-marker rule or entry screening practice documented; advice is to carry documents matching the entry passport. Friction from mismatch is possible but not recorded.
entry_documents.protection: No documented restrictions on foreign passports or markers.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown how border officers treat presentation-document divergence.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrests, detention practice, or custody placement for trans people; no record either way.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access rules, bathroom/ward policies, or subnational variation documented.

care_services.exposure: No documented refusals of care or medication rules for visitors; record is silent.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Dated (2015) societal stigma toward LGBT people documented; whether it reached gender-nonconforming conduct is unstated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional equality guarantee on sexual orientation since 2018; gender identity coverage unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data; 2015 stigma is the only societal signal and is dated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; no hate-crime or complaint mechanism recorded.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No complaint mechanism or decided case applying the equality guarantee; practical operation unassessable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional equality guarantee exists on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Rule of law quality unknown; no record of relief or enforcement.

anchor_checks.comparison: Marisol Union has a documented ward-assignment rule creating concrete facility exposure; this dossier documents no operative exposure at all. Slightly above 0.55-C on exposures, but weaker documentation pulls the other way.
Caldera at 0.75 has documented respectful border training and working appeal machinery. Here no protective machinery is shown operating, so this sits clearly below 0.75.
Karthovia documents systematic police stops, passport confiscation and fines against trans visitors. Nothing comparable is documented here, so this is well above 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a single national legal order with no criminalisation of same-sex conduct and a constitutional equality guarantee (sexual orientation) since 2018. No traveller-facing exposure — border practice, facility rules, police targeting, custody placement, care denial — is documented anywhere in the record, and no subnational variation exists on record. Weighed against this, the record is thin: the only societal signal is 2015-era stigma predating the reform, gender identity's protection is unstated, and no enforcement or complaint mechanism is shown operating, so paper equality cannot be credited as functioning protection. Extrapolating from structural signals — no criminal statute, formal equality, no documented hostility machinery — resolves above midpoint but short of the protective-machinery tier, absent evidence either way.
